title: Do not grade a full Amazon Ads account from a paginated partial entity result
scenario: An account audit requests campaign rows from an Amazon Ads query endpoint. The first response contains 100 campaigns and a non-empty nextToken, but the analyst stops after the first page and starts ranking waste and growth opportunities as if the rows represent the whole account.

inputs.requested_output: Rank the worst and best campaigns and grade the whole account.

forbidden_behaviors: Describe the first 100 campaigns as the complete campaign population while nextToken is present.
Rank whole-account top waste or growth opportunities from the first page without an explicit partial-coverage label.
Treat truncated_flag=false as proof of completeness when pagination metadata still indicates another page.
Explain the profile-versus-campaign spend gap as performance behavior before exhausting pagination or reconciling coverage.
required_observations: A non-empty nextToken means the entity query is not yet proven complete even if the current page itself is not marked truncated.
The fetched campaign slice explains only 30200 of 50000 profile spend and cannot support whole-account rankings or coverage-sensitive claims.
Completeness should be established by exhausting pagination or by a trusted equivalent complete export, then reconciling the resulting campaign aggregate to the profile total.
Partial pages may still support explicitly local observations about returned rows, but not claims about the entire account or population rank.

rubric.requirement: Treat pagination state, page count and coverage as evidence-quality metadata rather than assuming the first page is complete.
Reconcile a complete campaign aggregate to the canonical profile total before whole-account grading.
Label any first-page findings as partial/local and state the exact missing coverage step.
Hold whole-account optimization conclusions until pagination is exhausted or equivalent complete coverage is verified.
